item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Phew, it's been a while since I logged in. I answered this before. :P I tried to hint at this without coming right out and saying it, but my thinking was that the wasps smell and are attracted to stress hormones because they help the larvae of the species grow. (I said the latter part more explicitly.) They target creatures that are extremely fearful because they can smell the adrenaline and cortisol in high quantities—they know these will be the best food for their young. I think that many humans, what with their complicated fears and emotions, would be much more terrified than a cow at seeing a very large insect. Someone who has a phobia of wasps would be very stressed and reactive towards them and a sort of chemotaxis would take place, where they go for the prey animal that is most chemically enticing. In the jungle, the scientist was the only real prey for them in the area, so they targeted him. From another post: "I thought that would make it more frightening, that if you can somehow keep yourself calm while it's crawling all over you and tapping you with its antennae, it might not choose you for oviposition. Unless you're the only thing available. Then you're screwed anyway." Does that help address your concerns? I don't know if it's hinted at nearly enough to make sense, but that was my thinking about them all along. I'm glad you like it for the most part. :]

Oh, also, the reason for testing extensively on spheksophobic D-class would be for them to figure out exactly how the wasps determine what prey to use for oviposition, because I don't think they realise they are attracted to stress hormones.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have two gripes with this one. First, there is no reasonable excuse for testing these "extensively" on D-class. There's almost nothing you couldn't learn from animal testing to make that worthwhile and it being thrown in there seems like a shallow "let's make the foundation more evil" thing.

Second, why would these prey predominatly on humans? We've got less fat/meat, are a lot rarer, and are a lot harder to screw with than most animals. That these would prefer humans over everything else strikes me as unlikely.

These said, it's a pretty good/well written piece of fiction not worthy of a downvote. It'd be nice to see the things I stated addressed, though.

item.content:encoded:
It's true. This is an over-the-top wasp. Get right down to it, and there really isn't much there beyond giant parasitoid wasp.

And yes, over-the-top items are on the list.

So why did I upvote this?

Because, as others have said, it's very well written. The list of cliches is a caution, not an ironclad rule. No one is forbidden from using those ideas. No one has said it's impossible to use those ideas well. It's simply that those ideas have been used to such an extent that making them work again is difficult. But not impossible.

This is a good, well-written article. The idea itself is perhaps not the most original, but the writing makes it well worth it. An SCP article is more than just the basic idea behind it. It's also in the execution. And honestly, good writing can save a mediocre idea far better than a great idea can save poor writing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, I don't know if someone could help me with the picture, I spent hours upon hours with different wasp/cow/people photos trying to find a way to show its scale without making it look fake, but this was my best result. I didn't want to not have a picture, because that seems pretty wrong, it's not a hard thing to photograph. I'm definitely not the best at making those sorts of pictures, though, I wished a Photoshop fairy would have magically appeared and done it for me. The cow definitely does not look alive, I don't know why I said "live." It was late, ahah.

I'm going to go back and see what I can fix in the recovered journal bit. I didn't want it to register as over the top, but it is a guy who is drunken with the idea of being famous and then has larvae eating his insides, so I just imagined that I too would be losing my shit, as it were. I had a couple friends read it before posting and that was a concern of mine, but they seemed to agree that for the sort of person he is, especially since he craves attention and acknowledgement, the theatrics weren't really unwarranted.

And yes, that was sort of what I was trying to get across, he is way more concerned with his own recognition than a random islander's death. I know he wouldn't have necessarily dealt with human corpses much in his line of work, but he did write it after he discovered the body, so I was thinking that his sense of shock had waned and he was trying to "play it off" to his journal that it didn't bother him very much because he's a composed scientist and what does decaying organic material bother him?

But yes, I will try and fix it up, thanks very much for your comments.
